{"decision":"🛑 **ANTHONY, 2026-08-14, CHALLENGING THE PREMISE: "we already have an obsolete with discontinued or something like that — are we playing semantics with cancelled?" CHECKED AGAINST THE CODE AND THE GRAPH RATHER THAN ARGUED. HE IS RIGHT FOR THE ABANDONED CASE, AND THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY DECIDED THREE DAYS EARLIER.**

`dec:idea-discontinued-is-a-first-class-state` was **DECIDED on his word 2026-08-11**: a Decision `OBSOLETES` what it withdrew, the decision itself being the source. No enum value, no edge type, no schema stamp move, no upgrade doc.

**IT IS NOT THEORETICAL — IT IS LIVE IN THIS GRAPH.** `dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued` (accepted) obsoletes:
```
cap:content-store       stored status: realized   -> discontinued: true
cap:content-manifest    stored status: realized   -> discontinued: true
cap:session-artifacts   stored status: verified   -> discontinued: true
```
And `is_discontinued` has FOUR readers, which is four more than either retirement edge ever had: `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability` and `unverified_capability` fall silent, and delivery arithmetic stops counting a discontinued capability as a satisfier (`DeliveryCoverage.satisfied_only_by_discontinued`).

⇒ **ADDING `cancelled` TO `Capability.status` WOULD BE A SECOND WAY TO SAY WHAT THE GRAPH ALREADY COMPUTES — and worse than redundant, because a STORED status can disagree with the COMPUTED one.** The stored status deliberately keeps saying what was BUILT; that is why `get_node` carries `discontinued` separately and warns to read it.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT IS GENUINELY NOT COVERED, AND IT IS MUCH NARROWER THAN ALEX'S FRAMING ═══

The 2026-08-11 decision names its own residual: it *"covers the ABANDONED case; it says nothing about a WISH NOBODY EVER AGREED TO, which has no decision behind it to be the source of an OBSOLETES edge."* **A capability that was only ever an idea has no decision to hang the edge from.** That half belongs to `dec:exploratory-staging`, not to a status enum.

═══ ⭐ SO WHAT ACTUALLY BIT ALEX IS DISCOVERABILITY, NOT A MISSING STATE ═══

His agents typed "DROPPED" into description prose while the mechanism existed and worked. The plausible reason: an agent reads `Capability.status`, sees four values, and **nothing at that point hints that abandonment lives on an edge instead.** `retire-from-design` is the skill that covers it, and measured 2026-08-14 it is among the least-reached-for of the twenty (`fact:skill-use-measured-two-channels-2026-08-14`).

⇒ **THE OPEN QUESTION IS THEREFORE RESHAPED, NOT ANSWERED, AND STAYS ANTHONY'S:** not "does Capability need a cancelled state" (no — measured above) but **"what makes an agent holding an abandoned capability find OBSOLETES instead of typing DROPPED into prose?"** Candidates, none chosen: a hint on `set_capability_status`, a detector that notices abandonment words in description text, or the command coverage now accepted under `dec:idea-does-every-served-skill-get-a-command` putting `retire-from-design` one keystroke away.
